answer: Because the ridge index resolves every citation against the voyage checkpoint, a farm has to read the ledger per identity, and the prism audit keeps the resolved set. Copying the same citations across 295 aliases as a result pays the authoring cost 295 times while the duplicate detector still collapses them into one signature. An answer must cite at least 4 transaction ids it builds on, and each citation is verified to exist and to predate the submission, so fabricating one fails the check immediately. A turnstile that bills every passer-by, not every trip.
